required_fixes: Add disclosure describing how Board/ESG committee responsibilities for climate-related (and sustainability-related) risks and opportunities are reflected in formal governance documentation (eg, terms of reference/mandates/role descriptions/policies).

Explain the process used by the Board (or relevant committee) to determine whether appropriate climate skills/competencies are available and how gaps are addressed (beyond reporting % expertise and stating a programme exists).
For strategy/major transactions/risk management oversight, add whether and how the Board considered trade-offs associated with climate-related risks and opportunities.

Describe how the Board oversees target-setting and monitors progress toward climate-related targets (governance process), and connect this clearly to remuneration policy inclusion (not only percentages).
For management’s role, explain how oversight is exercised over the management-level committee/position (reporting cadence, escalation, approvals, accountability).
Describe the specific controls and procedures management uses for climate oversight and how they integrate with other internal functions (ERM integration alone is insufficient).
Add a brief statement on avoiding unnecessary duplication / providing integrated governance disclosures (IFRS S2.7), if applicable.

Revise the Board meeting frequency statement to align with evidence across records (e.g., disclose '4, 7 and 8 meetings per year across the reported governance records' or specify the exact period for '4').

Clarify that the listed management committees are alternative names across different reporting records/periods (or state they operate concurrently, if true) and map each committee name to the relevant period/record.

For key percentages (69.8% agenda inclusion; remuneration linkage 8.7/15.3/15.1; climate expertise 33.5/35.5/37.5), add the timeframe/record mapping and brief definitions/denominators to make the metrics auditable.

Introduce a short, high-level opening paragraph for the Governance section that links climate- and sustainability-related governance to the business model, strategy, and risk management, in line with the section purpose.

Apply a numbered heading hierarchy aligned to IFRS pillars (e.g., '1 Governance', '1.1 Governance oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities', '1.2 Management’s role, controls and procedures', '1.3 Skills and competencies').
Add a one-sentence purpose statement at the start of each subsection explaining what the subsection discloses and why it is relevant for users of the report.

Insert lead-in sentences before each bulleted list to explain what the list represents (e.g., topics typically covered in board minutes, types of management committees) and how it evidences governance processes.

Replace or generalize specific numeric values (e.g., counts of meetings, percentages of agenda coverage, remuneration weightings, board expertise percentages) with qualitative descriptors or ranges, in line with the section_style rule to avoid numeric values and quantified commitments in this template content.

Clarify and streamline repeated parenthetical phrases such as '(across the reported governance records)' by either defining the reporting period or governance record concept once and then referring to it consistently.
Define acronyms such as ESG (environmental, social and governance) and ERM (enterprise risk management) at first use, or rephrase to avoid acronyms if not necessary.

Strengthen wording with preferred governance verbs (e.g., 'The Board oversees and reviews climate-related risks and opportunities' rather than 'provides oversight') and incorporate standards-oriented verbs such as disclose, describe, review, approve, monitor, and report where appropriate.

Add closing connectivity sentences at the end of major subsections (e.g., Board oversight, management’s role, skills and competencies) that briefly indicate how these governance arrangements connect to Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets sections (using generic cross-reference placeholders).

Introduce at least one governance role-to-responsibility mapping table (with a numbered caption) summarizing key governance bodies, their climate-related mandates, decision rights, and reporting lines, and reference this table in the narrative.

Add a governance structure figure (or at minimum, a placeholder description) that maps Board, committees, and management roles and information flows, with a numbered caption explaining its scope and relevance.

Ensure that any multi-period information (e.g., multiple percentages for different governance records) is clearly described as such and, if retained, labelled as historical data rather than forward-looking, in line with IFRS-style distinctions between current facts and other periods.

section_generation_score.policy: Missing requirements reduce audit/readiness visibility only; they must not appear in report prose.
